title: ~ 주시겠어요? · 주문하고 요청하기
tip: 가게나 식당에서 무언가를 달라고 할 때 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 표현입니다. 끝에 please를 붙이면 더 공손해요. Can I have ~? 도 같은 뜻입니다.

items.en: Can I get some water, please?
alt: Can I have some water, please?

items.en: Can I get an iced americano, please?
alt: Can I have an iced americano, please?

items.en: Can I get a menu, please?
alt: Can I have a menu, please?
Can I see the menu, please?

items.en: Can I get a receipt, please?
alt: Can I have a receipt, please?

items.en: Can I get the check, please?
alt: Can I get the bill, please?
Can I have the check, please?
Can I have the bill, please?

items.en: Can I get this to go?
alt: Can I have this to go?
Can I get it to go?

items.en: Can I get a bag, please?
alt: Can I have a bag, please?

items.en: Can I get a large size?
alt: Can I get a large one?
Can I have a large size?

items.ko: 냅킨 좀 더 받을 수 있을까요?
items.en: Can I get some more napkins?
alt: Can I have some more napkins?

items.en: Can I get a window seat, please?
alt: Can I have a window seat, please?

chat.title: 카페에서 주문하기
chat.goal: 음료 하나와 디저트 하나를 주문하고, 영수증도 달라고 해 보세요.
chat.setting: You are a friendly barista at a small coffee shop. The customer has just walked up to the counter. Take their order, suggest a dessert, mention sizes, and handle payment and the receipt.

title: ~ 주세요 · ~하고 싶어요
tip: I'd like는 I would like의 줄임말로, I want보다 훨씬 공손한 표현입니다. 뒤에 물건이 오면 I'd like + 명사, 하고 싶은 행동이 오면 I'd like to + 동사로 말해요.

items.en: I'd like a cup of coffee.
I'd like to make a reservation.
I'd like to change my room.
I'd like to get a refund.
I'd like to try this on.
alt: I'd like to try it on.

items.en: I'd like to pay by card.
alt: I'd like to pay with a card.
I'd like to pay by credit card.
I'd like to pay with my card.
I'd like my steak medium, please.

items.en: I'd like to open an account.
alt: I'd like to open a bank account.

chat.title: 호텔 체크인
chat.goal: 체크인하고, 방 조건(창가·높은 층 등)과 결제 방법을 원하는 대로 말해 보세요.
chat.setting: You are a front desk clerk at a city hotel. A guest arrives to check in. Ask for their name and reservation, offer room options, and ask how they would like to pay.

title: ~해 주시겠어요? · 부탁하기
tip: 다른 사람에게 무언가를 해 달라고 공손하게 부탁할 때 씁니다. Can you ~? 보다 정중해요. 뒤에는 동사 원형이 옵니다.

items.en: Could you say that again, please?

alt: Could you speak a little slower?

items.en: Could you take a picture for me?
alt: Could you take a picture of us?
Could you take a photo for me?

items.en: Could you show me the way?
alt: Could you tell me the way?

items.en: Could you turn on the air conditioner?
alt: Could you turn on the AC?
Could you turn the air conditioner on?
Could you turn the AC on?

chat.title: 관광지에서 부탁하기
chat.goal: 사진을 찍어 달라고 부탁하고, 길도 알려 달라고 부탁해 보세요.
chat.setting: You are a friendly local person walking past a famous landmark. A tourist stops you. You are happy to help but sometimes speak a little fast, so the tourist may need to ask you to repeat or slow down.

title: ~가 어디예요? · 장소 묻기
tip: 찾는 장소 앞에 the를 붙여 Where is the ~? 라고 말하면 됩니다. 말할 때는 Where's로 줄여도 같아요.

items.en: Where is the nearest subway station?
alt: Where is the closest subway station?
Where is the nearest metro station?

chat.title: 쇼핑몰 안내 데스크
chat.goal: 화장실, 엘리베이터, 식당가 등 장소 두세 곳의 위치를 물어보세요.
chat.setting: You work at the information desk of a big shopping mall. A visitor comes to ask where things are. Give short, clear directions (floor, left/right, next to something).

title: ~를 찾고 있어요
tip: 물건, 장소, 사람을 찾고 있다고 말할 때 씁니다. 가게에서 점원이 May I help you? 라고 물으면 이 표현으로 답하면 돼요.

items.en: I'm looking for a smaller size.
I'm looking for a quiet cafe.
alt: I'm looking for a quiet coffee shop.
I'm looking for a place to live.

chat.title: 옷 가게에서
chat.goal: 찾는 옷을 설명하고, 사이즈나 색이 다른 것도 찾아 보세요.
chat.setting: You are a shop assistant in a clothing store. A customer is browsing. Ask what they need, show items, and ask about size and color.

title: ~ 있어요?
tip: 상대에게 무언가가 있는지 물을 때 씁니다. 여러 개 중 아무거나 있는지 물을 때는 any를 넣어 Do you have any ~? 라고 해요.

items.en: Do you have this in another color?
alt: Do you have this in a different color?

items.en: Do you have any rooms available?
alt: Do you have a room available?

items.en: Do you have a vegetarian menu?
alt: Do you have any vegetarian dishes?
Do you have a phone charger?

chat.title: 약국에서
chat.goal: 두통약이나 감기약처럼 필요한 물건이 있는지 두세 가지 물어보세요.
chat.setting: You are a pharmacist at a small pharmacy. A customer comes in looking for some items. Ask about their symptoms and say whether you have what they need.

title: ~가 있나요? · 있는지 묻기
tip: 어떤 장소나 상황에 무언가가 있는지 물을 때 씁니다. 근처를 물을 때는 near here, nearby, around here를 뒤에 붙여요.

items.en: Is there a bank near here?
alt: Is there a bank around here?

items.en: Is there a convenience store around here?
alt: Is there a convenience store near here?
Is there a convenience store nearby?

items.en: Is there a pool in the hotel?
alt: Is there a swimming pool in the hotel?
Is there a pool at the hotel?

items.en: Is there a bus to the airport?
Is there a good restaurant nearby?
alt: Is there a good restaurant near here?
Is there a good restaurant around here?

items.en: Is there a message for me?
alt: Are there any messages for me?
Is there any message for me?

chat.title: 호텔 컨시어지에게 묻기
chat.goal: 근처에 식당, 편의점, 공항버스 같은 것이 있는지 물어보세요.
chat.setting: You are a hotel concierge. A guest asks about the area around the hotel. Tell them what is nearby and how to get there.

title: ~할 거예요 · 계획 말하기
tip: 이미 정해 둔 계획이나 할 생각을 말할 때 씁니다. 말할 때는 I'm gonna로 줄여서 많이 발음해요. 뒤에는 동사 원형이 옵니다.

items.en: I'm going to meet my friend tomorrow.
alt: I'm going to meet a friend tomorrow.

items.en: I'm going to rest this weekend.
alt: I'm going to relax this weekend.

items.en: I'm going to study English every day.
I'm going to go to Japan next month.
alt: I'm going to visit Japan next month.

items.en: I'm going to cook at home tonight.
alt: I'm going to cook dinner at home tonight.
I'm going to cook at home this evening.
I'm going to start working out.
I'm going to start to exercise.

items.en: I'm going to take a taxi.
I'm going to go to bed early.
I'm going to buy a new phone.

chat.title: 동료와 주말 계획 이야기
chat.goal: 이번 주말과 다음 주에 무엇을 할 계획인지 두세 가지 말해 보세요.
chat.setting: You are a friendly coworker chatting with the user in the office kitchen on Friday afternoon. Ask about their weekend and next week plans, and share your own plans briefly.

title: ~ 어때요? · 제안하기
tip: 무언가를 제안하거나 상대 의견을 물을 때 씁니다. 뒤에 명사가 오거나, 행동이면 동사에 -ing를 붙여요. How about you? 는 '당신은요?'라는 뜻이에요.

items.en: How about a cup of coffee?

alt: How about going for a walk?

chat.title: 친구와 약속 잡기
chat.goal: 만날 시간, 장소, 할 일을 제안해서 약속을 정해 보세요.
chat.setting: You are the user's friend. You both want to meet this weekend but have not decided when, where, or what to do. Be a little picky so the user has to suggest options.

title: ~해 본 적 있어요? · 경험 묻기
tip: 상대가 무언가를 해 본 경험이 있는지 물을 때 씁니다. ever 뒤에는 과거분사(been, eaten, seen 등)가 와요. 가 본 적 있냐고 물을 때는 been to를 씁니다.

items.en: Have you ever been to Seoul?
Have you ever seen this movie?
alt: Have you ever watched this movie?

items.en: Have you ever missed a flight?
alt: Have you ever missed your flight?

items.ko: 그 사람 만나 본 적 있어요?
alt: Have you ever met that person?
Have you ever traveled by yourself?

chat.title: 처음 만난 사람과 대화
chat.goal: 상대에게 경험(여행, 음식, 취미 등)을 두세 가지 물어보세요.
chat.setting: You just met the user at a casual meetup. You are a curious traveler who has visited a few countries. Answer questions about your experiences and ask the user simple questions back.
